title: RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture and Phase 4 acceptance run
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the final acceptance gate.

Build a RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture in tests/fixtures/revengGraph.ts containing tmux_lib at tmux_lib, jfred/external/tmux_lib, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; two occurrences each of claude_plugin_lib and scenarios; nested submodules beneath ordinary directories; and distinct parent chains. Drive a full run against it in tests/revengEndToEnd.test.ts.

Verify in that fixture that a change originating from any repeated occurrence converges everywhere; all child and ancestor suites pass; approval precedes every commit, merge, and push; all occurrence histories consolidate into one operation per logical repository; gitlinks propagate through the correct explicit parents to the root; and every intended local base ends at the expected merge commit. Also verify no semantic commit, push, integration merge, base mutation, or archival occurs before approval, and that only successfully published tasks are archived.

Phase 4 acceptance: the recursive workflow is the production path, completes the RevEng-shaped run without data loss, and archives only tasks whose integration was successfully published.
problemSolvedByTask: Without an end-to-end fixture spanning repeated nested submodules, nobody can trust the recursive discovery/merge system before it becomes the production path for every real multi-repo task.

title: Give the codex reviewer sibling-task and blockedBy scope so chain boundaries read as intent
userDescription: verify.workflow.js should pass sibling-task scope (tasks owning overlapping files, plus the blockedBy graph) into the reviewer prompt, so codex stops flagging deliberate chain boundaries as omissions.
goal: - run-arguments.json carries a blockedBy array for every task that declares one
- the reviewer prompt names each sibling task sharing the group's files, by number and title
- the reviewer prompt states which tasks block, and are blocked by, the task under review
- a plan that leaves work to a named sibling or blocker is approved, not rejected as an omission
description:
The two halves start from different places, verified against a real run-arguments.json in the taskTools-86 worktree.

Sibling scope is already in hand: verify.workflow.js builds TASK_BY_NUMBER by flat-mapping every group's tasks, so each task and its files are reachable; codexPrompt simply never mentions them. Note that buildWorkflowArguments in scripts/prepareTasks.ts sets each task's files to the GROUP's union rather than the task's own declared files, so "tasks owning overlapping files" is exactly "tasks in the same group" — no new grouping logic is needed.

blockedBy is the missing half: buildWorkflowArguments emits only number, briefFile, planFile, and files per task, and the string blockedBy appears nowhere in the produced arguments. It must be carried through from the TaskRecord before verify.workflow.js can cite it.

Then extend codexPrompt to state the sibling list and the blocker relationships, and to say plainly that work assigned to a named sibling or blocker is out of scope for this plan and must not be reported as an omission. Pairs with task 120, which tells the same reviewer what is not grounds for rejection; this one supplies the scope facts that make those judgements possible.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

skills/tackle-tasks/verify.workflow.js was deleted (42ee3d3); the reviewer prompt now lives in scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexReviewBodyEmitter.ts (planReviewPrompt), spawned by scripts/tackle-tasks/codexReviewsPlan/CODEX_REVIEWS_PLAN.ts, with task data loaded by scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/preparedTask.ts (loadPreparedTask reads tasks.json directly). The claim that buildWorkflowArguments sets each task's files to the group union is false: scripts/prepareTasks.ts:375-427 builds one group per task with the task's own declaredFiles (pinned by tests/prepareTasks.test.ts:423). Sibling discovery must come from scripts/taskGroups.ts groupTasksByFileOverlap. TASK_BY_NUMBER and codexPrompt no longer exist in live code. Note: open task 157 renames the blockedBy key taskNum to taskNumber; plan against that rename landing.
tests: In tests/prepareTasks.test.ts assert buildWorkflowArguments carries blockedBy through. In a verify-workflow test, build fake ARGS with two same-group tasks and assert codexPrompt names the sibling and the blocker.
problemSolvedByTask: Codex needs to know if other tasks are related to the plan being reviewed, which might explain some of the plan's omissions found by codex, so that codex doesn't reject a plan for a reason that another task is meant to solve.

title: Second codex review only rechecks round-one findings instead of hunting for new ones
userDescription: the codex review prompt needs to indicate that a 2nd review by codex should only verify that the first round's flagged issues were resolved and not try to find new issues.  the purpose is to prevent a runaway review-reject-fix-review-reject-fix loop that happens often.
goal: - scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexReviewBodyEmitter.ts's reviewQuestion(t) always returns reviewByDefaultPrompt(t) for a non-scrapped plan, with no awareness of which review round is running.

- scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexTestReviewBodyEmitter.ts's reviewTestsQuestion(t, ...) has the same gap: it always returns reviewByDefaultPrompt(...), never the approve prompt already written beside it.

- reviewQuestion(t) must pick its prompt by round, using getAttemptCount(t.number, "planReview", t.taskStateRoot) from scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/taskRunState.ts, the same call TWO_CODEX_REVIEWS_COMPLETED_Q.ts already makes.
- reviewTestsQuestion(t, ...) needs the same round-aware selection for the tests review, so both reviewers stop always running a fresh full review with no memory of round one.
- On the first review pass, plan or tests, the existing full review prompt is unchanged: reviewByDefaultPrompt(t) for the plan, reviewByDefaultPrompt(...) for the tests.

- On the second pass, both functions instead return a recheck-only prompt carrying the user's proven wording: "check to see if ONLY the issues you flagged in the audit were resolved. Do not look for new issues in the descriptions."
- The plan recheck prompt points the reviewer at t.reviewOutputFile as the audit to recheck against; the tests recheck prompt points at t.testReviewFile.
- The existing checkpoint-based approve path in reviewQuestion(t), for a plan-scrapped relaunch, is untouched; the round check only governs the non-scrapped branch.

- The runaway loop stops reproducing: a task rejected in round one for reasons that were then applied no longer comes back rejected for a fresh set of issues in round two, for plan review or tests review.
- NOT in scope: regenerating the brief between review rounds or writing reviewer feedback back into tasks.json. This task only changes which prompt reviewQuestion and reviewTestsQuestion return.
- NOT in scope: naming which classes of issue are not grounds for rejection, such as nitpicks and code-fence language.
- NOT in scope: the sibling-task and blockedBy scope being added to the same reviewer prompt — task #155 owns that.
- NOT in scope: any test asserting the prompt wording. The user chose no test here because a prompt's instructions change often and such a test would only pin wording.
description: scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexReviewBodyEmitter.ts builds the plan review prompt: reviewQuestion(t) currently only branches on a plan-scrapped checkpoint, and otherwise always calls reviewByDefaultPrompt(t), the full review. scripts/tackle-tasks/codexReviewsPlan/CODEX_REVIEWS_PLAN.ts calls it through planReviewPrompt(t) with no awareness of which round is running. scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexTestReviewBodyEmitter.ts has the identical gap on the tests side: reviewTestsQuestion(t, ...) always calls reviewByDefaultPrompt(...), never the approveReviewByDefaultPrompt(...) already written next to it, and scripts/tackle-tasks/codexReviewsTests/CODEX_REVIEWS_TESTS.ts calls it through reviewTestsPrompt(t) the same way. That is the root cause on both sides — round two is a fresh full review with no memory of round one, so it is free to reject on problems it never raised before. The fix needs a second prompt on each side, not just changed prose, because prose alone cannot alter what the already-quoted codex exec command asks for. The counters for number of reviews already exist: scripts/tackle-tasks/whatIsReviewVerdict/TWO_CODEX_REVIEWS_COMPLETED_Q.ts reads getAttemptCount(t.number, "planReview", projectRoot) from scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/taskRunState.ts for the plan side, and scripts/tackle-tasks/areTestsFlagged/ARE_2_TEST_REVIEWS_DONE_Q.ts reads the task's codexReviewNotes field for the tests side. Round one's findings already land in a file next to the plan or the tests: t.reviewOutputFile (plan) and t.testReviewFile (tests) survive into round two untouched, so no new plumbing is needed to persist them, only a second prompt on each side that points the reviewer at that file instead of interpolating its contents into a shell command. This repo already carries tests for metacharacter-laden reason strings, so quoting arbitrary reviewer text into a command is a known hazard the file-based approach avoids. On round two, reviewQuestion(t) and reviewTestsQuestion(t, ...) must each emit a recheck-only prompt carrying the user's proven wording: "check to see if ONLY the issues you flagged in the audit were resolved. Do not look for new issues in the descriptions" — so a plan or a set of tests whose round-one items were fixed comes back APPROVED even when the reviewer could find something else. The existing two-review caps and the codex/fable/opus fallback chains in createCodexShellInvocationLive stay as they are; only which prompt each reviewQuestion function returns changes. Task #155 edits the same plan reviewer prompt for a different purpose, and groupTasksByFileOverlap will place both in the same worktree group, so no blockedBy is declared. No test pins the recheck prompt's wording — a prompt's instructions change often and such a test would only pin wording; tests stays "skip".
problemSolvedByTask: Codex is only told to "find issues", so it never checks if the plan amendments resolve the issues it found in the first round; instead codex only hunts for new issues.  Codex is really good at finding issues, which means the list of issues found never gets resolved and perpetually grows until codex ultimately rejects the plan.

title: 'changes detected' Stop hook prints the real staged diff
userDescription: make the 'changes detected' hook print out what changes are actually staged, because the agent's view of staged changes is always stale.  It should use the same code that the commit-message hook uses to provide the list of staged changes.
goal: - After a turn that edits and stages a file, the Stop hook's additionalContext contains the actual `git diff --staged` text for that file, not only the generic 'Files were changed' sentence.
- The staged-diff text comes from the same scripts/stagedDiffs.ts code path the commit-message skill uses; no second copy of the diff logic exists in the repo.
- The full diff is emitted, not a file-name-only list.
- Staged changes in a submodule whose pointer moved appear in the hook output, labelled per repo, the same way the commit-message skill labels them.
- `npm test` passes, including an updated tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts that asserts the staged-diff text is present in additionalContext.

- NOT in scope: changing the commit-message skill's own output or wording, changing the EXCLUDES list in stagedDiffs.ts, and changing the staging behaviour itself -- the hook still only reports, it never stages.
description:
The 'changes detected' hook is scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts (Stop/SubagentStop), which currently only checks `git status --porcelain` column two per file to decide if anything is unstaged, then emits a generic additionalContext string 'Files were changed. Stage the changes...' with no diff content. The commit-message skill already has the reusable staged-diff code in scripts/stagedDiffs.ts: it resolves the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from `process.cwd()`, runs `git diff --staged` with an EXCLUDES filter, and recurses into any submodule whose pointer moved. Note stagedDiffs.ts is currently a top-level script that writes to stdout, not an exported function -- confirm its actual shape in the source before assuming an export exists; extracting a reusable function is expected. stage-and-summarize-stop.ts must call that shared code and include the actual staged-diff text in the additionalContext payload instead of the generic reminder, so the agent sees what is really staged rather than trusting its stale in-context view. The user chose the FULL staged diff, not a file-name-only list, and chose reuse of the same code over a new lighter implementation. Complication: stage-and-summarize-stop.ts iterates over `paths` that can span multiple repos/submodules (using `dirname(p)` per path), while stagedDiffs.ts resolves only one repo root from cwd with no repo parameter, so this task must either loop the stagedDiffs logic per distinct repo root among the flagged paths, or add a repo-path parameter. tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts's `run()` helper currently asserts additionalContext matches /commit-message skill/ and does not exercise diff content, so the tests need updating to assert the emitted diff text appears in additionalContext.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

scripts/stagedDiffs.ts already exports stagedDiffs() (line 27) with a CLI guard at line 55 — the extraction this description asks to confirm is done. It takes no repo argument and resolves a single root from cwd; the remaining work is the repo-path parameter. 'The hook still only reports, it never stages' means not in scope for this task; task 160 owns staging behavior.
tests: Unit test on the hook: create a temp git repo, write and `git add` a file, feed scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts its Stop-hook JSON on stdin (with a turn-flag file listing that path), and assert the printed hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext contains the staged diff text for that file.
problemSolvedByTask: The agent doesn't accurately see what is really staged after the end-of-turn stage-and-summarize-stop.ts hook fires.

title: Store tasks in SQLite with tags so blockers and files are queries, not agents
userDescription: find a way to store tasks so that they're queryable so that an agent isn't needed to investigate open tasks that block and an agent isn't needed to find the files it touches.  probably needs some kind of tagging system per task/file.
goal: - A query script answers "what blocks task N" and "which open tasks touch file X" from the SQLite database, with no agent run
- A script regenerates a human-readable tasks.json from the database on demand, and the regenerated file matches what the database holds
- /create-task shows the derived tags for approval and accepts user-supplied tags instead
- createTask.workflow.js no longer spawns the blocker-hunter or file-hunter agents; it calls the query script
- The existing test suite still passes: npm test reports no failures after the storage swap
- NOT in scope: the .done file watcher handshake — task 187 owns that
description:
Move task storage from .taskTools/tasks.json to a queryable SQLite database at .taskTools/tasks.db. Use node:sqlite or bun:sqlite — already stdlib, so no new dependency. package.json has no "dependencies" key at all today, only @types/node.

Add per-task and per-file tags so 'what blocks task N' and 'which open tasks touch file X' are SQL queries instead of agent research. The query system should behave like the context-mode query system: structured lookups, not prose. Tags are derived automatically from what a task already has, then presented to the user for approval ("do these tags match? [list]"), with an optional "specify tags" path so the user can supply their own.

Keep a human-readable escape hatch: scripts/generateTasksJson.ts regenerates tasks.json from the database on demand, so a person can still read the task list until the SQLite version is fully integrated everywhere.

Then retire the research agents. skills/create-task/createTask.workflow.js currently spawns two parallel agent() calls through runWithFallback — file-hunter (FILE_HUNTER_SCHEMA: files/description/difficulty) and blocker-hunter (BLOCKER_HUNTER_SCHEMA: blockedBy). Both must be replaced with direct calls to the new query script, and skills/create-task/SKILL.md updated to match.

Existing code to rework: all task I/O funnels through scripts/taskFiles.ts (resolveTaskFiles, readTaskFile, seedTaskFilesIfAbsent) and scripts/appendTask.ts (appendTaskToTasksJson, buildTaskEntry), which read and write tasks.json as a flat JSON array of TaskRecord objects with fields taskNumber, title, userDescription, goal, description, files, tests, difficulty, blockedBy, chainGoal, handoffFilePaths. These become the database-backed read/write layer. scripts/checkBlockers.ts and scripts/getUnblockedTaskNumbers.ts do in-memory graph and cycle detection over blockedBy arrays loaded from tasks.json; that logic becomes SQL. scripts/getTaskDetails.ts, scripts/addTaskFiles.ts, scripts/nextTaskNumber.ts and scripts/closeTasks.ts all read or write tasks.json and must follow.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

'All task I/O funnels through scripts/taskFiles.ts and scripts/appendTask.ts' understates the blast radius: roughly thirty files read tasks.json directly (scripts/prepareTasks.ts, PREAMBLE_STATUS_CHECK.ts via jq, resetTask.ts, taskStats.ts, viewTaskHook.ts, and others). Per this task's own design the regenerated tasks.json stays authoritative for those readers; they are not migrated by this task.
tests: Seed a fixture task set into the database, run the query script for 'which open tasks touch file X' and 'what blocks task N', and assert the answers match hand-checked expected results, with no agent involved.
problemSolvedByTask: extracting information from tasks.json requires complex 'jq' expressions, vs. simpler SQL queries and table joins.

description:
Add a new /mermaid skill (skills/mermaid/SKILL.md, following the existing skill format seen in skills/view-task/SKILL.md and skills/create-task/SKILL.md) that searches a target codebase and emits a .mmd mermaid flowchart. ` line) rather than separate `_YES`/`_NO` boxes, a `classDef`/`class` block at the end assigning every box exactly one role among `script`, `returns_a_prompt`, `next_diagram`, `output`, and `fail`, and any box the diagram references but does not itself resolve grouped into a second `subgraph ... title: Read the diagram folder for tackle-tasks from .taskTools/settings.json
userDescription: The ability to define which set of diagrams to use for tackle-tasks.  this ability makes the skill and pipeline runner generic, allowing the end user to provide their own diagrams.  the default diagram would be the current pipeline.  .taskTools/settings.json is where this diagram setting would live.
goal: - With no .taskTools/settings.json, `/tackle-tasks [N]` runs the current pipeline block for block: the run-log's ran[] matches today's.
- With settings.json holding `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`, generateSteps, the workflow and the hook all read that folder; the run-log names that folder's blocks and none of the default pipeline's.
- A diagramFolder that does not exist or holds no .mmd stops the run at launch with a message naming the path. No fallback.
- Not in scope: a guide for users who author their own diagrams. A later task owns it.
description:
generateSteps.ts (invoked as `node scripts/generateSteps.ts diagrams/tackle-tasks` from package.json's "steps"/"steps:watch" scripts) resolves the diagram folder from process.argv, falling back to the dead default `plans/diagrams` (diagrams actually live at diagrams/tackle-tasks/*.mmd) when no CLI arg is given. It walks that folder into scripts/steps.json plus per-box stub scripts under scripts/tackle-tasks/, using a hardcoded BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER box-name map tied to the current pipeline's diagram set. generateWorkflow.ts and runStepHook.ts consume the already-generated scripts/steps.json and are diagram-folder-agnostic, so they don't need to change. No .taskTools/settings.json file or reader exists anywhere in the codebase yet (grepped scripts/, skills/, tests/) — this would be a new config file and a new settings-read helper, most naturally added in generateSteps.ts's CLI entrypoint (diagramFolder resolution) ahead of its current argv/hardcoded-default fallback, with the current diagrams/tackle-tasks folder becoming the default when no setting is present.

Setting shape settled with the user: `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`. The folder holds the .mmd files plus each block's script and template. An absent file or key means diagrams/tackle-tasks.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

User decision: both step consumers stay in the fence. scripts/runStepHook.ts and scripts/generateWorkflow.ts are owned so the merge fence cannot block this task, whichever consumer ends up edited. The setting may still flow only through regenerated scripts/steps.json (also owned), in which case the hook and workflow generator need no code change.
tests: A test writes .taskTools/settings.json naming a temp folder with one .mmd of two blocks and their scripts; runs /tackle-tasks; asserts the hook walked those two blocks and none of the default pipeline.
